_comment: Ground truth for the segmentation regression fixtures. Read the provenance
on every field before trusting it: the numbers here were counted BY HAND from
the photographs, on purpose. Recording them by running the pipeline instead
would make the test grade the implementation with itself, which is the one
thing a regression test must never do.
Each file is raw 8-bit single-channel luma, row-major, width*height bytes, no
header. Sources live in the archived scrivio_old repository.

toleranceSemantics.expectedLines: absolute; the test asserts count within +/- tolerance
toleranceSemantics.expectedWords: absolute; present only where the count was read with certainty
toleranceSemantics.mustNotDetect: no returned box may overlap any of these rectangles at all

fixtures.source: handwriting1.jpg — 3264x1836 phone photo of a lined notebook page, rotated in EXIF, dense Hebrew notes
fixtures.linesProvenance: Counted by eye from the photograph. A row-projection count over the text column independently gives 33. Treated as 33 +/- 3: the page is dense enough that a tighter claim would be false precision.
fixtures.wordsProvenance: DELIBERATELY ABSENT. Dense cursive-adjacent Hebrew with dashes and attached punctuation; hand-counting words at this resolution produces a number that is wrong for reasons unrelated to segmentation. Asserting it would fail the pipeline for the annotator's mistakes, not the pipeline's.

fixtures.source: handwriting2.jpg — NOT a photograph. A clean digital rendering of Hebrew text inside a rectangular frame (a title card).
fixtures.wordsProvenance: Exact. Crisp glyphs, read directly: title 'הפילה שהניאל כל כנור' = 4, attribution '[מתוך תמונות דף שו.]' = 4, then four body lines of 7, 7, 6, 4. Total 32.
fixtures.why: This is the fixture that can assert an exact word count, and it earns its place twice: it pins word grouping and reading order to an exact number, and it is the control that proves the two photographs' looser tolerances are not hiding a pipeline that has stopped working.

fixtures.source: handwriting3.png — 1591x2096 phone photo of a lined notebook page, dense Hebrew notes, three punched holes down the left margin and a column of names written in the right margin
fixtures.linesProvenance: Counted by eye from the photograph, including the faint header lines and the right-margin name column. A row-projection count over the text column gives 42. Treated as 40 +/- 4.
fixtures.wordsProvenance: DELIBERATELY ABSENT — same reason as handwriting1.
fixtures.mustNotDetectProvenance: Located objectively by connected-component labelling of the dark mask in the left margin: three components of ~1800 px each, 47x49, 49x49 and 47x49. The rectangles are those bboxes grown by 6 px. These are not holes the pipeline should 'reasonably' reject on size — at 1800 px they are 0.1% of the frame, well under maxBlobAreaFrac. Rejecting them requires the line-height filter to work, which is precisely why they are in the fixture.
